description: Per-stage request lifecycle latency broken down by Kafka API key.

panels.title: Conduktor Gateway Lifecycle - by API key

options.content:
This dashboard breaks down the Conduktor Gateway request lifecycle **per API key**, so you can see which clients (Kafka API keys) drive latency at each processing stage. Read more in [Gateway request lifecycle metrics](https://docs.conduktor.io/guide/conduktor-in-production/monitor/gateway_lifecycle_metrics).

Each row is one lifecycle span, identified by its checkpoint range (T0 to T10):

- `preprocess` (T0 -> T1) - decode, authenticate and prepare the incoming request
- `authorization` (T1 -> T2) - ACL authorization check
- `request.interceptor` (T2 -> T3) - run request interceptors (aggregated across all interceptors)
- `request.rebuilder` (T3 -> T4) - rebuild the request for the upstream broker
- `upstreamqueue` (T4 -> T5) - time queued before being sent upstream
- `upstreamwait` (T5 -> T6) - waiting for the Kafka broker to respond
- `response.rebuilder` (T6 -> T7) - rebuild the broker response for the client
- `response.interceptor` (T7 -> T8) - run response interceptors (aggregated across all interceptors)
- `response.authorization` (T8 -> T9) - response-side ACL authorization check
- `response.send` (T9 -> T10) - encode and send the response back to the client
- `total` (T0 -> T10) - end-to-end time spent inside Gateway

Within each row, the three panels show **mean** latency, **max** latency and **rate** (samples/s), with one line per API key. Use the **pod** and **API key** dropdowns above to filter which pods and API keys are shown.

The `request.interceptor` and `response.interceptor` rows aggregate all interceptors for each API key; for a per-interceptor breakdown, see the **Lifecycle - by Interceptor** dashboard.

Note: a missing or zero series means traffic for that API key did not reach that stage - for example, produce requests with `acks=0` skip all response spans and the `total` span.

panels.description: Mean latency by api_key for preprocess (T0 -> T1).

targets.expr: sum by(api_key) (rate(gateway_request_preprocess_duration_seconds_sum{job="$job", pod=~"$pod", api_key=~"$api_key"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by(api_key) (rate(gateway_request_preprocess_duration_seconds_count{job="$job", pod=~"$pod", api_key=~"$api_key"}[$__rate_interval]))
